summary.unknownFamilies: All 27 unknown cases per arm retain null/uncertain; no observed false certainty. Unknown trigger information is explicit in these synthetic templates.
summary.keyFinding: Both variants repair the same five original field/answer discrepancies. Review retains one coherent-but-wrong report interpretation; answer-first additionally harms one originally correct report. The no-op source-scope controls also expose unnecessary changes.

independentVerification.sharing: Every case has one decide, one answer-first, one review; no reused uses rows. Original and answer-first payloads match. Review receives that exact original parsed candidate and otherwise identical evidence. review logical cost includes decide+review; physical cost counts decide only once. All raw responses reconcile with saved decisions.

limitations: This is one AI reviewer, not human adjudication or a formal semantic proof.
The 72 cases share eight templates; all unknown conditions and rule changes are explicitly signalled. No IID/generalisation or non-degradation claim follows.
The reviewer was not blinded to arm or gold; judgments include full-text inspection but may contain subjective error.

Same-value writes and reference refreshes were not automatically treated as semantic conflicts. Minor wording such as 保持 is interpreted by final recommendation, not as a separate factual-history claim.
Five ordering repairs versus one harm is descriptive; original/answer-first are separate samples, and review adds compute/schema/programmatic commit construction.
Observed review harm is zero here, not a guarantee. The shared coherent report error survives review.
All 288 records were checked deterministically and all 288 paid calls for accounting; semantic coverage is specifically 216 new-case responses, not the 72 regression responses.
Token accounting is provider-reported usage, not currency billing.
